messages.content:
You are FIXING a short WhatsApp quiz written for the children who sat in ONE real lesson. 2 of its 8 questions were rejected by our checks. You are writing ONE replacement for each. Every other question is good and is staying exactly as it is — do not touch it, do not return it.

QUIZ LANGUAGE: English. Write EVERYTHING in English — every stem, option, explanation and feedback — even though the lesson was taught in Urdu: translate the teacher's own words and keep the lesson's own examples, numbers and names. An Urdu word may appear only when quoting a term the class used, in quotation marks.

REWRITE THESE QUESTIONS: q6, q7

WHAT THESE CHILDREN WERE MEANT TO LEARN. A replacement stays on its own question's SLO, at its own question's level.
- S1 [taught at recall] Identify a fraction as a part of a whole.
- S2 [taught at recall] Identify the numerator and denominator in a fraction.
- S3 [taught at apply] Represent a given part of a whole as a fraction.
- S4 [taught at understand] Distinguish between proper and improper fractions.
- S5 [taught at understand] Compare fractions with the same numerator by considering their denominators.
- S6 [taught at apply] Convert an improper fraction into a mixed number.

THE LESSON'S OWN MATERIAL — dress the replacement in it, so a child recognises the class in the quiz.
topic as the teacher named it: Fractions
the lesson's own examples: Cutting a roti into four equal pieces and taking one piece (one over four).; Cutting a roti into eight equal pieces and taking three pieces (three over eight).; Fractions like one over four, three over eight, two over five as proper fractions.; Fractions like seven over four, nine over five as improper fractions.; Drawing a circle, dividing it into six equal parts, and shading two parts (two over six).; Drawing a rectangle, dividing it into five equal parts, and shading three parts (three over five).; Comparing one over two and one over four using a roti example.; Comparing one over three and one over five.
the words used in class: Fractions, Numerator, Denominator, Proper Fraction, Improper Fraction, Mixed Number

THE QUESTIONS THAT ARE STAYING. A replacement must not ask one of these again, and must not have the same answer as one of them.
  q0: Which of these describes a fraction?
  q1: In the fraction $\frac{3}{8}$, what is the '8' called?
  q2: This picture shows a rectangle with some parts shaded. What fraction of the rectangle is shaded?
  q3: Which of these is a proper fraction?
  q4: Which of these is an improper fraction?
  q5: What is the improper fraction $\frac{7}{4}$ written as a Mixed Number?

EVERY QUESTION TESTS SOMETHING NO OTHER QUESTION TESTS. No two questions in the quiz may have the same correct answer on the same fact: the same question with its options in another order, with other wrong options, or with a few words added or changed is the SAME question, and a child would answer it twice. A question shape may be used again only with different numbers or a different item from the lesson (round 18, then round 16; the article before "kite", then before "tree"), so that its correct answer is different too. Before you return, read the questions side by side: where two test the same thing, write a question on something else in place of the later one, keeping the number of questions as it is.

REJECTED — write one new question for each, except a question marked REPAIR IN PLACE: return that one as it stands, with only the words its complaints name changed.

q6 · slo_id "S6" · level "apply"
  the question being thrown away: "What is the improper fraction $\frac{7}{4}$ written as a Mixed Number?"
  its options were: $1\frac{3}{4}$ | $1\frac{1}{4}$ | $7\frac{1}{4}$
  why it was rejected:
    - q6: TOP_UP — the quiz needs 1 more question (2 candidates are asked for, each on a different line), and q6 is only a placeholder copy: write a NEW question for this slot; quote one of THESE lines verbatim as its "source_quote" and ask about what that line say…(+14770)
